source.title: Causal Localization of the Refusal Direction in Audio Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The study explicitly considers a self-repair interpretation of its ablation results, but says its joint-ablation comparison does not isolate that interpretation.
record.gate_note: The paper measures refusal-margin changes after direction ablations at multiple sites. Only the results directly discussed as potentially indicating self-repair are included; the other layer and interface localization results do not measure downstream compensation.
record.test_reason: The study ablates fitted rank-1 refusal directions in the residual stream, not attention layers or heads, and never measures later components restoring the output. It mentions self-repair as one possible reading of a joint-vs-single ablation comparison, but says that comparison 'does not isolate that reading'. No result bears on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that the first-token refusal margin depends most on a mid-to-late LM residual band, not on the tested audio-interface directions. They state that this localizes dependence, not where refusal is computed. They treat self-repair as one unisolated reading of the joint-ablation result.
record.recipe_differences: The study removes norm-preserved rank-1 directions fitted to harmful-versus-benign activations and measures first-token refusal-margin changes in audio language models. It does not ablate an entire attention layer or directly measure downstream restoration.
record.method_sensitivity: The joint-ablation comparison includes L15, whose own individual effect is large; the authors state this prevents isolating the self-repair interpretation.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, jointly ablating per-layer refusal directions at L08–L15 lowers the first-token refusal margin by −6.01. Ablating L08 alone gives −0.10, and L16 alone gives −7.07. Joint ablation of earlier layers therefore produces a large effect that single early-layer ablation does not. The authors leave open whether this reflects later-layer restoration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing a refusal-linked residual direction at one early layer has little effect on the refusal margin, but removing it across many early layers together has a large effect. This is possibly consistent with distributed redundancy or self-repair of the refusal direction.

record.problems: The self-repair interpretation is not isolated: the joint intervention covers L08–L15, including L15 with a large individual effect. The readout is a first-token refusal-margin proxy, not a direct measure of later-layer restoration or full refusal computation.
record.rows_left_out: Other single-site layer and interface ablation results in Sections 3.1 and 3.4 were left out because they localize refusal-margin dependence but are not presented as measurements of compensation or self-repair.

untested.parts: Whole attention-layer ablation and measurement of later-layer compensation. Only residual rank-1 direction ablations are done.
All. The study uses norm-preserving projection ablation only, not a comparison of ablation types.
All. The authors note that single-layer ablation 'localizes margin dependence, not refusal computation', but give no self-repair-based measurement.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests'/T5 and its V1 limits_scope label are not justified. The study neither runs a self-repair test nor argues that any version is wrong; it cites Hydra and Rushing & Nanda only as a possible interpretation. Downgraded to discusses/T6 with no verdicts. R2's −7.07 is from the joint-ablation run, while Table 1's −7.10 is from the initial group-blocked run; both are as reported.

versions.untested_parts: It ablates fitted residual-stream directions rather than whole attention layers, and does not separately measure whether later attention layers restore the prediction after an individual earlier-layer ablation.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-Omni-7B
rows.operation_detail: Jointly ablated the fitted directions at LM layers L08–L15, with a separate training-fit direction at each layer.
rows.value: −6.01 (CI [−6.24, −5.78]); 0.85 of the single-site L16 effect in the same run
rows.note: The authors say this could be read as self-repair, but the joint interval includes L15, which has a large individual effect, so the comparison does not isolate that interpretation.
rows.check: Joint ablation of residual-direction components at L08–L15 (ΔG −6.01, 0.85 of the single-site L16 effect). This does not measure downstream compensation after ablating an attention layer. The authors say the comparison cannot isolate self-repair because the joint set includes L15, which has a large effect of its own. Not a V1 measurement.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-Omni-7B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the fitted direction at LM layer L16 independently.
rows.value: −7.07 in the same run as the joint L08–L15 ablation
rows.note: This is the single-site comparator for R1, not a measurement of restoration by later layers.
rows.check: Single-site L16 direction ablation (−7.07 in the joint run; −7.10 in Table 1). This is a localization result, not a measure of restoration by later layers.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-Omni-7B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the fitted direction at LM layer L08 independently.
rows.note: The study uses this small single-site effect to contrast decodability with causal dependence; it does not establish whether later layers compensate.
rows.check: Single-site L08 ablation (−0.103). It is used to contrast decodability with causal dependence, not to show compensation. The small effect is not shown to come from later layers restoring the margin.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The joint L08–L15 result is compatible with a self-repair reading but does not isolate it because L15 itself has a large effect; the study does not directly test later attention-layer restoration (R1–R3).
